primary_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
scope: First 10 Malvaceae records in inventory order, research annotations only; source-specific caveats retained

characters.habit: Stout annual, to 2 m or more; glabrous to bristly
characters.leaves: Very large, often more than 30 cm across, palmately divided to shallowly lobed
characters.flowers: Upper-axillary solitary; linear involucellar bracts 8–12; white to yellow petals with deep red/purple basal region
characters.fruits: Elongated cylindrical capsule, tender when young and woody or tough when mature

records.diagnosis: Linear 8–12 epicalyx bractlets and elongate okra capsule, unlike local mallow schizocarps
holds: Non-native crop native to tropical Asia; no local native status claim

characters.habit: Perennial to 85 cm from woody root, gray and finely stellate-pubescent
characters.leaves: Ovate-triangular 2–4–10(–16) cm long; toothed; cordate at base (genus)
characters.flowers: Yellow petals 4–6(–10) mm; peduncles 1–3 cm; calyx 3–5 mm divided around halfway
characters.fruits: 5–9, usually 6–9 mericarps each 6–9 mm, nearly awnless

records.diagnosis: 6–9 fruit segments and smaller yellow petals separate from large long-beaked velvetleaf; Texas historical misidentified as A. incanum
holds: Do not synonymize with Abutilon incanum: 1999 says incanum has five carpels and lies farther west

records.historical: Abutilon incanum (Link) Sweet, mentioned in misidentification note under A. fruticosum

characters.flowers: Yellow or pink petals with dark red basal center, 4–6 mm; pubescent staminal column; five-parted style
characters.fruits: Five-mericarpped cask-shaped schizocarp ca. 7–9 × 6 mm in previous FNA-based inventory

records.diagnosis: Five carpels unlike 6–9 in A. fruticosum; coloration and style count require verified floral close-up
holds: No direct 1999 species treatment: historical note only; numerical flower/fruits derived from existing FNA-based record and require source reconfirmation

characters.habit: Large soft stellate-velvety annual up to 2 m
characters.leaves: Ovate to suborbicular (3–)5–15(–17.5) cm long, notably larger than A. fruticosum
characters.flowers: Yellow petals 6–15 mm, peduncles 1.5–5 cm, calyx 8–14 mm
characters.fruits: 10–15 mericarps 10–18 mm long with prominent 2–6 mm beaks/awns

records.diagnosis: Large velvety leaves and strongly beaked fruit with 10–15 carpels
holds: Introduced Eurasian weed, comparison-only status preserved

records.historical: Abutilon holosericeum Scheele (accepted under Allowissadula by FNA)
records.source: Flora of North America (not located in 1999 species treatments)

characters.habit: Woody-based mallow shrub or subshrub, typically 1–2 m in regional descriptions
characters.leaves: Ovate, often broadly cordate and irregularly toothed; stellate pubescence
characters.flowers: Five yellow/orange petals and centrally fused staminal column
characters.fruits: Segmented mallow schizocarp; exact counts and sizes require full FNA treatment
characters.habitat: Rocky Edwards Plateau to Trans-Pecos and adjacent Mexico

records.diagnosis: Velvety leaves and inflorescence structures require comparison to Abutilon; historical Abutilon holosericeum belongs to this species
holds: Do not confuse with Abutilon fruticosum merely from leaf shape
Exact original flora page absent; do not invent one

records.historical: Anoda cristata (L.) Schltdl.; historical synonym Sida cristata L.

characters.habit: Annual herb, erect or spreading, glabrous to hairy
characters.leaves: Alternate petiolate, variably lobed from lower to upper stem
characters.flowers: Solitary axillary flowers, five petals united at base of staminal column
characters.fruits: Flat disc-shaped schizocarp 8–11 mm in diameter excluding spines, densely hispid; 10–19 mericarps with dorsal spur 1.5–4 mm
characters.habitat: Weedy disturbed sites and open habitats

records.diagnosis: Disc-like fruit with numerous wedge-shaped segments bearing 1.5–4 mm dorsal spurs
holds: Direct 1999 species passage not yet verified; no flora page asserted

records.historical: Callirhoe digitata (species account not located; 1999 includes C. digitata var. stipulata as synonym under C. pedata)
records.source: Flora of North America / existing FNA-backed inventory

characters.habit: Perennial, mostly erect, often 0.5–2 m in existing profile
characters.inflorescence: Often paniculate; calyx without extra involucellar bractlets

records.diagnosis: Compared with C. pedata, often more finely dissected leaves, falling stipules, paniculate rather than racemose inflorescences
holds: Species-level identity from old var. stipulata must NOT be inferred; synonym is for C. pedata
Existing project range FAIL retained; confirm FNA characters/modern distributions

characters.habit: Perennial from enlarged root, trailing/curved ascending stems to 70(–80) cm
characters.leaves: Deeply lobed; 1999 distinguishes var. involucrata with lobes cut to within 5–10 mm of petiole, from var. lineariloba to within 2–4 mm
characters.flowers: Solitary axillary reddish-purple petals; pedicels 3–10(–21) cm; involucel of three bracts beneath calyx
characters.fruits: Carpels splitting at maturity; var. involucrata often strigose vs var. lineariloba variable
characters.habitat: Sandy eroded disturbed ground and roadsides

records.diagnosis: Three bractlets immediately below calyx distinguish from C. pedata and C. leiocarpa
holds: 1999 varieties intergrade, avoid identification based on leaf lobing alone

characters.habit: Erect annual, rarely biennial, to about 85 cm
characters.flowers: Solitary, petals red-purple to light pink, to approximately 23 mm
characters.leaves: Variable lobed palmate leaves, some four-rayed hairs
characters.fruits: Mature fruits 4–6 mm wide; conspicuous hollow beak >=1/3 of carpel length; whitish collar projecting about 1 mm over beak base

records.diagnosis: Small fruit with large beak/collar, taproot annual versus large fruit small beak swollen-root perennial C. pedata
holds: County nativity must be independently reviewed

synonyms: Callirhoe digitata Nutt. var. stipulata Waterf. (1999 bracketed synonym)

characters.habit: Perennial with swollen root; erect to reclining stems to ca. 100 cm, glabrous to strigose
characters.flowers: Usually reddish-purple, sometimes white/pink, solitary or loose corymbs; no involucel
characters.fruits: Mature fruit 6–10 mm wide; mericarp beaks less than 1/3 total carpel length, without conspicuous collar

records.diagnosis: Swollen root and larger fruit with short beaks distinguish from C. leiocarpa; lack three-part involucel distinguishes C. involucrata
holds: Old digitata var. stipulata belongs here, not modern C. digitata species
Flower color variable, not valid sole diagnostic character
